subject: math.GR
name: Lagrange theorem
statement: If G is a finite group and H is a subgroup, then |G|=[G:H]|H|. In particular, the order of every element divides the order of G.

subject: math.GR
name: Cauchy theorem
statement: If a prime p divides the order of a finite group G, then G contains an element of order p.

subject: math.GR
name: Sylow theorems
statement: Write the order of a finite group G as p^a m, with p prime and p not dividing m. Subgroups of order p^a exist and are all conjugate; every p-subgroup is contained in one, and their number divides m and is congruent to one modulo p.

subject: math.GR
name: Jordan-Holder theorem
statement: Any two composition series of a group have the same length and the same simple factor groups up to isomorphism and permutation. A composition series is a finite subnormal series whose successive quotients are simple.

subject: math.GR
name: First isomorphism theorem
statement: For a group homomorphism f:G to H, the kernel is normal in G and the quotient G/ker(f) is naturally isomorphic to the image of f.

subject: math.GR
name: Cayley theorem
statement: Every group G is isomorphic to a subgroup of the permutation group of its underlying set, via left multiplication. In particular, a group of order n embeds in the symmetric group S_n.

subject: math.GR
name: Orbit-stabilizer theorem
statement: For a group G acting on a set and an element x, the orbit of x is in bijection with the left cosets of its stabilizer G_x. For finite G this gives |Gx|=|G|/|G_x|.

subject: math.GR
name: Class equation
statement: For a finite group G, |G|=|Z(G)| plus the sum of [G:C_G(x)] over one representative of each noncentral conjugacy class. Here Z(G) is the center and C_G(x) is the centralizer of x.

subject: math.GR
name: Burnside orbit-counting lemma
statement: If a finite group G acts on a finite set X, the number of orbits equals (1/|G|) times the sum, over g in G, of the number of elements of X fixed by g.

subject: math.GR
name: Burnside p^a q^b theorem
statement: Every finite group whose order is p^a q^b, with p and q prime and a,b nonnegative integers, is solvable.

subject: math.GR
name: Feit-Thompson theorem
statement: Every finite group of odd order is solvable.

subject: math.GR
name: Schur-Zassenhaus theorem
statement: If N is a normal subgroup of a finite group G and |N| is relatively prime to [G:N], then N has a complement H: G=NH and N intersect H is trivial. All such complements are conjugate in G.

subject: math.GR
name: Hall theorem for solvable groups
statement: Let G be a finite solvable group and pi a set of primes. G has a Hall pi-subgroup, whose order has only prime divisors in pi and whose index has none; all such subgroups are conjugate, and every pi-subgroup lies in one.

subject: math.GR
name: Nielsen-Schreier theorem
statement: Every subgroup of a free group is free. If a subgroup has finite index d in a free group of finite rank r, then its rank is 1+d(r-1).

subject: math.GR
name: Kurosh subgroup theorem
statement: A subgroup of a free product of groups is itself a free product of a free group and subgroups of conjugates of the original factors. The factor subgroups can be chosen using representatives of the appropriate double cosets.

subject: math.GR
name: Structure theorem for finitely generated abelian groups
statement: Every finitely generated abelian group is isomorphic to Z^r direct sum a finite collection of finite cyclic groups. It has a unique invariant-factor description Z^r direct sum Z/d_1Z direct sum ... direct sum Z/d_sZ with 1<d_1 dividing d_2 dividing ... dividing d_s.

references.title: Structure theorem for finitely generated abelian groups

subject: math.GR
name: Malcev residual finiteness theorem
statement: Every finitely generated subgroup of GL_n(k), for a field k of characteristic zero, is residually finite. Thus each nonidentity element survives in some finite quotient of the subgroup.

subject: math.GR
name: Tits alternative
statement: Every finitely generated subgroup of GL_n(k) over a field k either contains a nonabelian free subgroup or has a solvable subgroup of finite index.

subject: math.GR
name: Gromov polynomial growth theorem
statement: A finitely generated group has polynomial growth if and only if it contains a nilpotent subgroup of finite index. Polynomial growth means that the number of elements expressible by words of length at most n in a finite generating set is bounded by a polynomial in n.

subject: math.GR
name: Schur finiteness theorem
statement: If the quotient of a group G by its center is finite, then the commutator subgroup of G is finite.
